in_text_mentions: By immunofluorescence and laser scanning confocal microscopy, the positive staining of IgG, C5b-9, C4d, C3d, C1q, MBL, factor B and properdin was further confirmed on the glomeruli of patients with anti-GBM disease (Figure 3).

IgG co-localized with C3d exactly along the GCW (Figure 3A–C). C1q, factor B and properdin co-localized with C5b-9 exactly along the GCW too (Figure 3D–L). panels.rationale: Single light-microscopy image of a human renal biopsy (PAS-type stain) without panel letters, treated as panel A. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Human kidney biopsy (PAS, ×200) from a patient with confirmed anti-GBM disease showing cellular/fibrocellular crescents and necrotic glomerular capillary walls, the classic renal manifestation of anti-GBM disease. B: Immunofluorescence of a human kidney biopsy showing smooth linear IgG deposition along glomerular capillary walls, the pathognomonic hallmark of anti-GBM disease; in-text confirms 'The findings confirmed anti-GBM disease.' C: Second human kidney biopsy (Elastica-Masson, ×200) from the same anti-GBM patient showing fibrous crescents, globally sclerotic glomeruli and diffuse tubulointerstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy; this is chronic sequelae of anti-GBM disease, not a control or other disease.

in_text_mentions: Kidney biopsy at 16th day showed cellular or fibrocellular crescents with or without necrotic glomerular capillary walls in 19 of 22 glomeruli (86.3%) (Figure 2(a)). There were diffuse inflammatory cell infiltration, patchy tubular injury, and mild fibrosis in the tubulointerstitial areas (Figure 2(a)). Immunofluorescence for IgG showed 2+ linear staining along the glomerular capillary walls (Figure 2(b)). The findings confirmed anti-GBM disease.
